phrase: I hope this email finds you well.
useCase: Opening a professional email with a courteous and standard greeting
example: Hi David, I hope this email finds you well. I'm writing to follow up on our conversation from last Thursday regarding the partnership proposal.
practicePrompt: You're writing a follow-up email to a business contact. Open with a professional greeting using this phrase.

useCase: Stating the purpose of an email when requesting information
example: I'm writing to inquire about the availability of your consulting services for a project we're launching in Q3.
practicePrompt: You need information from a potential service provider. State your purpose using this phrase.

phrase: Please find the attached document for your review.
useCase: Directing the recipient's attention to an attached file
example: Please find the attached document for your review. It contains the updated project scope and revised timeline we discussed.
practicePrompt: You're sending a revised proposal to a client. Reference the attachment using this phrase.

phrase: I wanted to follow up on my previous email regarding...
useCase: Sending a follow-up email when there has been no response to an earlier message
example: I wanted to follow up on my previous email regarding the contract renewal. Have you had a chance to review the terms?
practicePrompt: You sent an email last week but haven't received a reply. Follow up politely using this phrase.

phrase: Thank you for your prompt response.
useCase: Acknowledging and appreciating a quick reply from the recipient
example: Thank you for your prompt response. The information you provided helps us move forward with the planning process.
practicePrompt: A colleague replied to your email much faster than expected. Acknowledge their responsiveness using this phrase.

phrase: Could you please confirm receipt of this email?
useCase: Asking the recipient to acknowledge that they received and read the email
example: I've included the meeting agenda below. Could you please confirm receipt of this email so I know it didn't end up in your spam folder?
practicePrompt: You're sending an important document and need to make sure it was received. Request confirmation using this phrase.

phrase: I'd appreciate it if you could get back to me by...
useCase: Setting a polite but clear deadline for a response
example: I'd appreciate it if you could get back to me by Friday close of business so I can finalize the report over the weekend.
practicePrompt: You need an answer before the end of the week to proceed with your work. Set a response deadline using this phrase.

phrase: Please don't hesitate to contact me if you need any further information.
useCase: Closing an email by offering additional support or clarification
example: The attached report covers all the key metrics. Please don't hesitate to contact me if you need any further information.
practicePrompt: You're sending a detailed report to a client. Close the email by offering further help using this phrase.

phrase: I'm forwarding this email for your reference.
useCase: Sharing a previously sent email with a new recipient for their awareness
example: I'm forwarding this email for your reference. It contains the original discussion about the policy changes that affect our department.
practicePrompt: You want to share an important email thread with a colleague who wasn't originally included. Introduce it using this phrase.

phrase: Looking forward to hearing from you soon.
useCase: Closing an email with a warm expectation of a reply
example: I believe this arrangement would be mutually beneficial. Looking forward to hearing from you soon.
practicePrompt: You've proposed a meeting time to a client. Close the email with a positive expectation using this phrase.
